title: Plan map navigator search box does nothing
body:
## Summary
The Project Map navigator shows a "Search features (Cmd+K)..." input that has no value, no onChange and no Cmd+K binding (src/components/modules/core-engine/PlanMatrixMap/Sidebar.tsx:36).

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/PlanMatrixMap/Sidebar.tsx:36-40 renders an uncontrolled <input> with no handler; grep for metaKey / 'k' under PlanMatrixMap/ returns 0 hits, so the advertised shortcut does not exist either. Typing filters nothing on a 240-node map. Fixed looks like: a query state in usePlanMatrixMap that dims non-matching nodes through nodeOpacity (the same mechanism filterModuleId uses) and Enter selects/zooms the first match; or remove the input. Which of the two is the product choice; the dim+select build is inside the context's declared purpose.

## Flow
- open Implementation Plan -> Matrix map
- type a feature name into the navigator search
- observe: nothing on the canvas changes; Cmd+K does nothing

## Expected impact
Users looking for one feature among 240 nodes get a working find; could break nothing outside the map.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the map search finds features
Before: 0 handlers on the input, 0 Cmd+K bindings; typing changes 0 nodes
After: predicted: query dims non-matching nodes (240 -> N matching at opacity 1)
Method: simulation - walked the render path; the S instrument (render map, type, count opacity-1 nodes) was not built this round
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/components/modules/core-engine/PlanMatrixMap/Sidebar.tsx:36-40 <input type="text" placeholder="Search features (Cmd+K)..." className=.../> (no value/onChange)
grep -rn "metaKey\|'k'" src/components/modules/core-engine/PlanMatrixMap -> 0
instrument: component test: render PlanMatrixMap with a mocked plan, type a featureName, count nodes rendered at opacity 1 (expect 240 before, matches after)

title: Plan map nodes cannot be reached or selected without a pointer
body:
## Summary
The 240 feature nodes on the plan map are plain divs with onClick only - no tabIndex, role or key handler (src/components/modules/core-engine/PlanMatrixMap/CanvasNodes.tsx:34).

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/PlanMatrixMap/CanvasNodes.tsx:34 and :98 render each node as a <div onClick> (0 tabIndex/role in the file). The canvas surface has keyboard pan/zoom (src/components/modules/core-engine/PlanMatrixMap/Canvas.tsx keydown) but no way to move focus to a node, so the DetailPanel and its Implement button are pointer-only. registry canvas-graph/canvas-accessibility: one tab stop for the surface plus topological (arrow along edges) or spatial roving focus, and an announced selection. Fixed: roving focus within the canvas (Arrow keys move between nodes in the same row/cluster, Enter opens DetailPanel), aria-activedescendant or a single focused node.

## Flow
- Tab to the map canvas
- try to reach any node with the keyboard
- observe: only pan/zoom keys work; no node can be selected

## Expected impact
Keyboard and screen-reader users can open feature details and build from the map; could break pointer hover/selection if the roving state fights hoveredKey.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - nodes reachable by keyboard
Before: 0 of 240 nodes focusable or selectable by key
After: predicted: all 240 reachable via roving focus, Enter selects
Method: simulation - read the render path; needs an M build plus a keyboard test
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: component test: focus the canvas, press ArrowRight/Enter, assert DetailPanel opens for the expected node; pair with the existing combo-chain-graph-node-keyboard.test.tsx pattern

title: Genre DNA timeline end labels overlap when confidences are close
body:
## Summary
GenreDnaTimeline places each strand's right-hand label at its latest y with no collision avoidance, so patterns with similar latest confidence print on top of each other (src/components/modules/core-engine/GenreDnaTimeline.tsx:154).

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/GenreDnaTimeline.tsx:154 labelY = clamp(last.y + 3); plotH = 200px for 0-100, so 1 confidence point = 2px and a 9.5px label overlaps any neighbour within ~5 points. With 13 possible patterns (PATTERN_COLORS) and two patterns at 0% latest (both clamp to the bottom) overlap is the common case, not the edge. Fixed: a pure label-layout pass (sort by y, push apart to a min gap of ~11px, clamp to the plot) with a leader line when moved.

## Flow
- history with two patterns ending at 40% and 42%
- render the timeline
- observe: both labels drawn within 4px - unreadable

## Expected impact
Creators can read which strand is which in the Evolution tab; could shift labels away from their strand ends (leader lines mitigate).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every end label legible
Before: simulation: labels for 40% and 42% at y 4px apart (< 11px glyph height); any two 0% patterns at identical y
After: predicted: min label gap >= 11px for any input
Method: simulation - three walked inputs; the S instrument is a pure layout helper + test
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/components/modules/core-engine/GenreDnaTimeline.tsx:37-39 H=240, PAD top 14 bottom 26 -> plotH 200
src/components/modules/core-engine/GenreDnaTimeline.tsx:154 const labelY = Math.max(PAD.top + 4, Math.min(H - PAD.bottom - 2, last.y + 3));
instrument: extract layoutEndLabels(ys, minGap, top, bottom) and test min pairwise gap over generated inputs; render test counting label y gaps

title: Genre DNA timeline data is hover-only
body:
## Summary
Per-pattern first/latest/delta figures appear only on mouseenter of an SVG group; the chart is one role="img" with a generic label (src/components/modules/core-engine/GenreDnaTimeline.tsx:128).

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/GenreDnaTimeline.tsx:128 aria-label="Pattern confidence over time" is the only text a screen reader gets; the readout at :210 renders only while hovered (set by onMouseEnter at :158). No keyboard path and no tabular fallback. Fixed: a visually-hidden table (pattern, first, latest, delta) or focusable legend entries that set hovered on focus.

## Flow
- open Evolution tab with >= 2 scans
- navigate with keyboard / screen reader
- observe: only "Pattern confidence over time" is announced; no values

## Expected impact
Non-pointer users get the drift numbers; could break nothing visual if the table is sr-only.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - values reachable without a pointer
Before: 0 of N pattern readouts reachable by keyboard/AT
After: predicted: N of N via focusable labels or sr-only table
Method: simulation - render path read
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/components/modules/core-engine/GenreDnaTimeline.tsx:128 role="img" aria-label="Pattern confidence over time"
src/components/modules/core-engine/GenreDnaTimeline.tsx:158 onMouseEnter={() => setHovered(pattern)} (no onFocus)
instrument: render test: assert each pattern name and its first/latest figure are present in accessible text without hover

title: Build session reports a failed run as "callback missing"
body:
## Summary
usePlanDispatch hands onSettled only (landed, callbackStatus), so useBuildSession reconstructs success as `landed || callbackStatus !== 'confirmed'` and a run that failed without a callback stops with the wrong reason (src/components/modules/core-engine/ImplementationPlan/useBuildSession.ts:116).

## Description
src/hooks/usePlanDispatch.ts:55-63 computes landed = success && confirmed and drops success. src/components/modules/core-engine/ImplementationPlan/useBuildSession.ts:116 then sends success = true for (success=false, callbackStatus=undefined), and src/lib/implementation-planner/build-session.ts:179-180 names it "callback missing" instead of "run failed". The door's own lastError (usePlanDispatch.ts:60) says "run failed" for the same event, so the page shows two different reasons for one failure. Fixed: onSettled carries success; the session passes it through.

## Flow
- start a build session
- the CLI run fails (success=false) with no callback
- observe: session says "Stopped at X: callback missing"; door error says "run failed"

## Expected impact
Operators see the real stop reason; touches the shared usePlanDispatch signature (3 consumers).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one truthful stop reason
Before: walked: (success=false, status=undefined) -> session reason "callback missing", door reason "run failed" (2 reasons for 1 event)
After: predicted: both "run failed"
Method: simulation - walked the three functions; usePlanDispatch.ts is outside this context
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: extend build-session-panel.test.tsx: fire onComplete(false, undefined) and assert "Stopped at X: run failed"

title: Feature-key short-name helper is copied in 4 places
body:
## Summary
`key.slice(key.indexOf('::') + 2)` is re-declared in usePlanDispatch, useBuildSession, BuildSessionPanel and inline in DetailPanel; PlanItemRow re-splits '::' twice more.

## Description
Copies: src/hooks/usePlanDispatch.ts:36, src/components/modules/core-engine/ImplementationPlan/useBuildSession.ts:49, src/components/modules/core-engine/ImplementationPlan/BuildSessionPanel.tsx:15, src/components/modules/core-engine/PlanMatrixMap/DetailPanel.tsx:144 (inline); split variants at src/components/modules/core-engine/ImplementationPlan/PlanItemRow.tsx:93,120 and src/components/modules/core-engine/PlanMatrixMap/DetailPanel.tsx:88,118 (the latter leaves an unused 'mod' - 2 lint warnings). The feature-key format is owned by feature-definitions ('moduleId::featureName'); one exported featureKeyName()/splitFeatureKey() in plan-generator would be the authority.

## Flow
- export splitFeatureKey from src/lib/implementation-planner/plan-generator.ts
- replace the 4 copies and 4 split sites
- pin with a unit test incl. a featureName that itself contains "::"

## Expected impact
One place to change if the key format grows; removes 2 lint warnings. Risk: a call site that relied on split vs indexOf semantics for names containing "::".

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one authority for the key format
Before: 4 helper copies + 4 split sites, 2 unused-var warnings
After: predicted: 1 helper, 0 copies, 0 warnings
Method: probe - grep count on the real tree; the change touches a hook outside this context
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: grep count of indexOf('::') / split('::') in the plan files (8 -> 0) + unit test of the helper

title: Plan map ignores the table's effort and impact filters
body:
## Summary
The Implementation Plan's FilterBar (module / max effort / min impact) narrows only the table; the embedded map calls useImplementationPlan() unfiltered and only fades by module (src/components/modules/core-engine/PlanMatrixMap/usePlanMatrixMap.ts:26).

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/ImplementationPlan/index.tsx owns the filter; src/components/modules/core-engine/PlanMatrixMap/usePlanMatrixMap.ts:26 opens its own unfiltered plan, and nodeOpacity (:214) knows only filterModuleId and critical path. Switching views silently drops "Trivial effort, High+ impact". Whether the map should honour the filters (fade or hide) or deliberately show the whole graph as context is a product call.

## Flow
- set Max effort = Small, Min impact = High+ in the table
- switch to Matrix map
- observe: all 240 nodes at full opacity

## Expected impact
Consistent scoping between the two plan views; could hide dependency context users rely on in the map.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - one scope across plan views
Before: table honours 3 filters, map honours 1 (module, as fade)
After: decision needed: fade vs hide vs ignore
Method: simulation - read both views; the benefit is a product preference
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence:
src/components/modules/core-engine/PlanMatrixMap/usePlanMatrixMap.ts:26 const { plan, loading, error } = useImplementationPlan();
src/components/modules/core-engine/PlanMatrixMap/usePlanMatrixMap.ts:214 nodeOpacity: filterModuleId / criticalPathMode only
instrument: operator decision on map semantics, then a render test counting faded nodes under a filter

title: Plan view tab bar has no tab semantics
body:
## Summary
PlanView's Plan/Evolution switcher is two plain buttons with the active state drawn as a coloured underline - no role="tablist"/"tab", no aria-selected (src/components/modules/core-engine/PlanView.tsx:60).

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/PlanView.tsx:35-48 and the TabButton at :60-83 expose 0 roles/states; the repo already ships an underline tab primitive (ui/TabBar) used elsewhere. Fixed: render the two tabs through ui/TabBar (role tablist/tab, aria-selected, arrow-key roving) or add the roles + aria-selected + aria-controls in place.

## Flow
- open Core Engine Plan view
- screen reader on the tab strip
- observe: two unrelated buttons, no selected state announced

## Expected impact
AT users know which panel is shown; risk is the visual change if ui/TabBar styling differs.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - tab state announced
Before: 0 role=tab, 0 aria-selected on 2 tabs
After: predicted: 2 role=tab, aria-selected on the active one
Method: probe - read the file; reuse decision (ui/TabBar vs in-place roles) left to the builder
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: render test: getAllByRole("tab") length 2 and aria-selected follows the click

title: Plan map uses 29 raw palette classes instead of theme tokens
body:
## Summary
The plan map's chrome hard-codes text-gray-*/text-white/bg-blue-600/text-blue-200 (29 occurrences across 5 files) instead of text-text / text-text-muted / accent tokens, so it ignores the theme.

## Description
Counts: src/components/modules/core-engine/PlanMatrixMap/DetailPanel.tsx 13, index.tsx 9, CanvasClusters.tsx 3, CanvasSectors.tsx 3, CanvasNodes.tsx 1. The rest of the context uses text-text / text-text-muted / surface tokens; registry design-tokens: semantic tokens over palette literals. Fixed: map each literal to its semantic token (text-white -> text-text, gray-300/400 -> text-text-muted(-hover), bg-blue-600 -> the core accent via MODULE_COLORS.core).

## Flow
- grep text-gray-|text-white|bg-blue-600|text-blue-200 in PlanMatrixMap/
- replace with semantic tokens
- visual check in light and dark theme

## Expected impact
Map chrome follows the theme like the table beside it; risk: contrast shifts on the dark canvas surfaces.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - token adoption
Before: 29 palette literals in PlanMatrixMap/
After: predicted: 0
Method: probe - grep count on the real tree; a visual check is needed before landing
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: grep -c "text-gray-\|text-white\|bg-blue-600\|text-blue-200" PlanMatrixMap/*.tsx -> DetailPanel 13, index 9, CanvasClusters 3, CanvasSectors 3, CanvasNodes 1
instrument: grep count 29 -> 0 plus a screenshot pair (light/dark) of the map

title: Plan map lets a build start while the page's session is running
body:
## Summary
Now that the map builds through the page's one door, its Implement button is still enabled while the Build session (or a row build) is running on that door (src/components/modules/core-engine/PlanMatrixMap/DetailPanel.tsx:143).

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/PlanMatrixMap/DetailPanel.tsx:143 gates only on item.isReady; src/components/modules/core-engine/ImplementationPlan/index.tsx knows isRunning from usePlanDispatch but does not pass it to the map, and usePlanDispatch.dispatch (src/hooks/usePlanDispatch.ts:74) overwrites inFlight without checking isRunning - a second dispatch mid-run re-targets the in-flight item so the first run's callback settles the wrong item. Fixed: pass isRunning to PlanMatrixMap and disable Implement with a "a build is running" reason; or refuse in the door.

## Flow
- start a Build session in the table
- switch to Matrix map, select a ready node, click Implement Feature
- observe: a second execute fires; inFlight now points at the map item

## Expected impact
No overlapping builds on one CLI session; the door-level guard would also cover the row Build button.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - one build in flight per door
Before: walked: 2 executes accepted while isRunning=true; inFlight overwritten
After: predicted: second dispatch refused with a named reason
Method: simulation - walked dispatch/inFlight; a door-level fix touches src/hooks (outside this context)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/hooks/usePlanDispatch.ts:81 inFlight.current = item; (no isRunning check)
src/components/modules/core-engine/PlanMatrixMap/DetailPanel.tsx:143 disabled={!item.isReady}
instrument: usePlanDispatch test with isRunning=true: second dispatch returns not-ok and execute count stays 1
